planting.note: Space fans 18-24 inches apart in full sun; tall 40-inch scapes carry saturated orchid-purple, ruffled flowers over a chartreuse throat.

directions: Plant divisions in spring in full sun and well-drained, fertile soil, spacing clumps 18 to 24 inches apart to give the tall 40-inch scapes room to show off their ruffled blooms. Hybridized by Robert P. Selman and registered with the AHS in 2026 from a cross of Alienation and Alien Angel, this tetraploid opens saturated orchid-purple flowers with a chartreuse throat. Keep soil evenly moist through the midseason bloom flush and divide congested fans every three to four years to maintain vigor.

planting.note: Space fans 18-24 inches apart in full sun; semi-evergreen tetraploid with lavender-pink flowers and a magenta-etched lavender-blue eye.

directions: Set divisions 18 to 24 inches apart in full sun; this semi-evergreen tetraploid tolerates average garden soil as long as drainage is good. Robert P. Selman registered Eyeronic with the AHS in 2026, breeding it out of the Over the Rainbow Bridge line to produce lavender-pink flowers with a vivid lavender-blue eye and a gold-filigreed magenta edge. Water regularly during the early-midseason bloom period and mulch lightly in colder zones to protect the evergreen-leaning foliage.

planting.note: Space fans 18-24 inches apart in full sun; peach-pink flowers with a patterned lavender-violet eye and ruffled partial picotee edge.

directions: Give this 28-inch-tall semi-evergreen tetraploid full sun and consistent moisture during its midseason bloom window, spacing fans 18 to 24 inches apart. Robert P. Selman registered the cultivar with the AHS in 2026 out of a Garden Gnome cross, producing peach-pink flowers with a patterned lavender-violet eye and a ruffled partial picotee edge. Fertilize lightly in spring and divide crowded clumps every few years to keep bloom counts high.

planting.note: Space fans 18-24 inches apart in full sun; salmon-pink flowers veined darker with a raspberry eye and gold-trimmed ruffled edge.

directions: Plant in full sun with rich, well-drained soil, allowing 18 to 24 inches between fans so the 26-inch midseason scapes can branch freely. This tetraploid, registered by Robert P. Selman with the AHS in 2026 from an Elgar Enigma Variations cross, carries light salmon-pink petals veined darker with a raspberry eye and gold-trimmed ruffled edge. Keep the semi-evergreen foliage watered through summer heat and divide every three years to renew vigor.

planting.note: Space fans 18-24 inches apart in full sun; late-season pale fuchsia flowers with a violet-etched lavender-blue watermark and white picotee edge.

directions: Site this 28-inch late-blooming tetraploid in full sun and well-drained soil, spacing divisions 18 to 24 inches apart. Robert P. Selman bred and registered Sotto Voce with the AHS in 2026 from a Denim Sky cross, giving pale fuchsia flowers a lavender-blue watermark etched in violet and a ruffled white picotee edge. Water deeply during dry spells and lift and divide crowded clumps in spring every three to four years.

planting.note: Space fans 18-24 inches apart in full sun; fragrant diploid with burgundy petals, a dark band, and greenish-yellow throat.

directions: Grow this compact, fragrant diploid in full sun with evenly moist, well-drained soil, spacing fans about 18 to 24 inches apart to let the 27-inch scapes show off their early-midseason blooms. Rebecca Harding Hartigan registered Googly Bear with the AHS in 2026 from a cross of Everybody Loves Tim and Northwood Tie Dye Artist, producing burgundy petals with a dark band and greenish-yellow throat. Divide every three years once clumps become congested to keep flowering strong.

planting.note: Space fans 18-24 inches apart in full sun; dormant diploid with lavender petals, a purple eye, and green throat, 21 buds per scape.

directions: Plant this dormant diploid in full sun and fertile, well-drained soil, spacing clumps 18 to 24 inches apart to support its tall 36-inch scapes. Bred by Bret Clement and registered with the AHS in 2026, Mental Floss carries lavender petals around a purple eye and green throat, and reblooms later in the season when deadheaded and kept watered. Divide congested fans in early spring every three to four years to sustain its heavy 21-bud count.

planting.note: Space fans 18-24 inches apart in full sun; dormant diploid with yellow flowers patterned with a purple eye over a yellow-green throat.

directions: Give this dormant diploid full sun and well-drained soil, spacing fans 18 to 24 inches apart beneath its 38-inch midseason scapes. Hybridizer Bret Clement registered the cultivar with the AHS in 2026 from an Electric Snake cross, producing yellow flowers patterned with a purple eye over a yellow-green throat. Water consistently through bloom season and divide crowded clumps every few years to maintain vigorous flowering.

planting.note: Space fans 20-26 inches apart in full sun; dormant diploid with red flowers, darker veining, and a yellow-green throat, 21 buds per scape.

Bret Clement bred and registered Incriminating Evidence with the AHS in 2026, producing red flowers with darker veining over a yellow-green throat that rebloom when spent scapes are trimmed back. Water deeply during the midseason-to-late bloom flush and divide congested clumps every three years.

planting.note: Space fans 18-24 inches apart in full sun; dormant diploid with unusually formed yellow flowers, a red feathered eye, and green throat.
